description.narrative:
Proposed project is contributing to the Oxfam Somali country program’s wider support to climate action civil society organizations (CSO) to establish a country wide climate action CSO network that is regionally and globally linked with likeminded networks.The project will support Somali CSOs to continue ongoing dialogues, consensus building, actualizing establishment a nationwide climate action network with its sub-national chapters at Benadir regional administration, Galmudug, Hirshabelle, Jubbaland, Puntland and South-West State as well as Somaliland1 level. Before March 2025, a network of estimated 250+ CSO spread across 902 districts will be established and launched.
CSOs are essential actors in climate action in Somalia. They bridge the gap between international initiatives and national and local realities, ensuring that climate strategies are rooted in the needs and knowledge of the Somali communities. By mobilizing communities, advocating for policy changes, implementing projects, and fosteringcollaboration, CSOs play a pivotal role in building resilience and promoting sustainable development in the face of climate change. Their work is crucial for mitigating and adopting the impacts of climate change and ensuring that the most vulnerable populations in Somalia are not left behind. Somali CSO’s meaningful engagement in the climate action requires technical capacity, improved legal and policy frameworks, consultative national processes, coordination and communication mechanisms, access and participation, joint monitoring and evaluation mechanisms, and internal organizational capacities within CSOs.
To realize the potential of CSOs in climate action, there is a felt need of a collective and collaborative platform at national and sub-nationallevel (as a first step towards further localizing we aim at federal members states). This platform is for CSOs to engage in a consistent and regular manner and enable CSOs to contribute constructively to climate action related processes in Somalia.
Oxfam and a group of local partners have first time discussed the felt need of Somali CSO platform during the consultative and preparatory meetings for United Nations Climate Change Conference or Conference (COP28) last year. This year, discussions have expanded at Somali NGO Consortium and Climate Change, Resilience <(>&<)> Adaptation Working Group level (plesae refer to Annex 1 for list of Somali CSOs involved in initial discussions). Establishing network at national and sub-national level is best achieved if resources are pulled together by mutual interest sharing organizations. Welthungerhilfe (WHH -is current co-chair of Climate Change, Resilience <(>&<)> Adaptation Working Group) and Danish Refugee Council (DRC) came onboard and in principle agreed to join efforts to support Somali CSOs in establishing the network. Based on discussions so far, we have chalked out below initial concepts and actions to actualize the idea and agreed to start mobilizing initial required resources – including initial investment funding
Envisioning network A voluntary structure of climate, environmental and sustainable development oriented CSOs in Somalia whose work parallels at least one of the programmatic pillars of Somali Climate Action related policies and acts. Strive to have maximum possible geographical spread across the country (due to various territorial disputes, administrative unclarity etc. this is challenging part of nationwide network). • Committed to build Inclusive network – organizations representing minority clans, people with disability, women rights organizations, displaced people’s associations, youth organizations etc. • Embrace a ‘whole-of-society approach’ for climate action. Participatory and transparent decision-making process. Be credible voice of Somali people. • Advocate for increasing allocation of financial resources at local (below sub-national e.g., region and districts) and bottom-up decision making and planning. • Important in Somali context to have ‘conflict-sensitive climate financing mechanisms’ • Collaboration to accelerate and focus on the urgent delivery of the 2030 climate goals. Mobilize required resources and capacities – including technical capacities.
The initial funding from Oxfma Ireland will enable Oxfam Somali program to systematically extend its efforts to Somali CSOs to actualize above listed initial ideas and concepts into establishment of platform – while continue working with them to further mobilize required resources – including technical, managerial and financials.

participating-org.narrative: In 2004 Oxfam Novib set up a Liaison Office in Nairobi, Kenya in order to support the Strengthening Somali Civil Society Program, at the request of the EU. This request was based on Oxfam Novib's work in Somalia to date, but intended to be more widely directed atthe entire civil society sector and the specific context in which it is operating in a post-conflict country. The program started with consulting local organisations in Somalia and Somaliland to get a complete picture of the sectors and regions where they are active, the challenges they face and the relationship between civil society, local political structures and the private sector. A program was then developed to strengthen the institutional development of Oxfam Novib's partners and those of other Oxfams, as well as a range of new NGOs. In the first year local consultants were trained in Somalia. They were then seconded to civil society organisations to build their capacity in financial and organisational management. Furthermore, workshops were organised on specific themes suchas human rights and the role of civil society in the Somali context. The Liaison Office is now going to support the expansion of the program, focussing on strengthening both organisation and project management, while facilitating more training in the fields of civic education, governance, human rights and women's rights, HIV and AIDS and child protection. Over the years, the Somalia Country Office has expanded its intervention on short term humanitarian response as well as development development interventions. In 2015/2016, a decision was reached to move the Country Programme operation, which was largely in Nairobi, from Nairobi to Hargeisa. The country office has a small office in Nairobi , Kenya and large operations office in Hargeisa, Somaliland.
